macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stock futures slip as investors await Fed minutes
items.summary: S&P 500 and Dow futures fell about 0.2%, while Nasdaq futures declined roughly 0.3% as rising Treasury yields and Wednesday’s Federal Reserve meeting minutes weighed on sentiment.[2]

items.title: Soft jobs report reduces October Fed hike expectations
items.summary: September U.S. payroll growth of 29,000 and a rise in unemployment to 4.2% sharply reduced market expectations for another Federal Reserve rate increase this month.[1][3]

items.title: Treasury yields remain elevated
items.summary: The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield was around 5.27%, while the 30-year yield stood near 5.63%, keeping bond-market pressure in focus for equities.[2]

items.title: Asian markets advance; European trading mixed
items.summary: Japan’s Nikkei gained about 2% and broader Asia-Pacific markets rose, while France’s CAC 40 fell 0.8%, Germany’s DAX edged up 0.1%, and the U.K.’s FTSE 100 gained 0.3%.[1][2]

items.title: RXO shares jump after C.H. Robinson acquisition deal
items.summary: RXO shares rose more than 20% in premarket trading after C.H. Robinson Worldwide agreed to acquire the logistics company in a cash-and-stock transaction valued at about $5.8 billion.[2]

items.title: Oil prices remain volatile
items.summary: U.S. crude fell about 0.5% to $90.68 a barrel, while Brent crude rose roughly 0.7% to $102.91 as energy markets weighed supply and demand developments.[2]

items.title: Fed minutes and weekly earnings calendar in focus
items.summary: Investors are awaiting Wednesday’s minutes from the Fed’s September meeting. Constellation Brands, Levi Strauss, PepsiCo, and Delta Air Lines are among the prominent companies scheduled to report this week.[1][3]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rises above $86,000 as crypto market capitalization tops $3 trillion
items.summary: Bitcoin climbed about 2.1% over 24 hours to roughly $86,436, while Ethereum rose 1.4% to about $2,727. The global cryptocurrency market capitalization increased 0.8% to approximately $3.01 trillion; Bitcoin liquidations totaled about $52 million amid the rally.

items.title: OKX and ICE parent file for tokenized stock-trading platform
items.summary: OKXICE, a joint venture between OKX and Intercontinental Exchange, reportedly applied to the SEC to launch a platform offering tokenized versions of 63 NYSE-listed companies. The proposal would operate under the SEC’s new innovation exemption and preserve shareholder rights such as voting and dividends.

items.title: SEC chair signals additional cryptocurrency rules
items.summary: SEC Chair Paul Atkins said more cryptocurrency regulations would be introduced to support the goal of making the United States a global crypto hub. The announcement comes as policymakers consider clearer frameworks for digital-asset markets and custody.

items.title: Ethereum Glamsterdam upgrade scheduled for Sepolia testnet
items.summary: Ethereum’s Glamsterdam upgrade is scheduled to activate on the Sepolia testnet on October 6. Mainnet and Hoodi dates have not been set, and no action is required from ETH holders.

items.title: Zcash activates faster-block upgrade on public testnet
items.summary: Zcash’s NU7 upgrade, including 25-second blocks, went live on its public testnet ahead of schedule. The project is targeting a November mainnet deployment.

items.title: Ronin announces Karst upgrade activation
items.summary: Ronin’s Karst upgrade is scheduled to activate on October 7, with users not expected to take action. Wallet users affected by the Waypoint migration have been told to move assets by October 16.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Krafton cancels PUBG: Black Budget
items.summary: Krafton and PUBG Studios reportedly cancelled development of the extraction-shooter spin-off PUBG: Black Budget.

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 reveals DMZ trailer
items.summary: Microsoft released a new trailer focused on the DMZ mode for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, which is scheduled for October 23 on PC, Xbox Series X|S, PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch 2.

items.title: Gears of War: E-Day sets series Steam concurrency record
items.summary: Gears of War: E-Day reportedly exceeded 20,000 concurrent players during early access, setting a new Steam peak for the franchise ahead of its full release.

items.title: Ghost of Yotei complete edition launches on PlayStation 5
items.summary: Sony released a complete edition of Ghost of Yotei for PlayStation 5, bundling the base game with the Echoes of Sekigahara story expansion.

items.title: ARC Raiders announces free-play weekend
items.summary: The developers of ARC Raiders announced a promotion allowing everyone to play the game for free during the following weekend.

items.title: New games release this week
items.summary: This week’s notable releases include Gears of War: E-Day, Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen, Kingdom Hearts Collection [I–III], Earth Defense Force 5 for Nintendo Switch 2 and Star Wars: Galactic Racer.

items.title: Psikyo Memories announced for PS5 and Switch 2
items.summary: Psikyo Memories will bring 12 classic shoot-’em-ups to PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch 2 on February 18, 2027, with standard and special editions planned.

items.title: Tim Sweeney warns of severe games-industry crisis
items.summary: Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney said the traditional games industry is approaching a serious downturn, comparing current conditions with the major video-game-market crash of the 1980s.
